title: Building a RAG Pipeline on SQL Server

questions.q: The chapter describes five pipeline stages. Which four live in SQL Server, and which is the only external stage?
options: Chunking, embedding ingestion, retrieval, and prompt assembly stay in the database; only the LLM generation call leaves it
Ingest, embed, and retrieve are external; only prompt assembly and generation are in-database
All five stages run inside SQL Server via sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint
Chunking is external; embedding, retrieval, assembly, and generation are in-database
questions.explain: Stages 1–4 (ingest/chunk, embed, retrieve, assemble) run in SQL Server — so permission filtering happens in the retrieval procedure — and only stage 5, the LLM generation call, leaves the database.

questions.q: The retrieval procedure uses TOP_N = @TopK * 5 in VECTOR_SEARCH. Why over-fetch, and when should the trim to @TopK happen?
options: Over-fetch 5x to survive permission and publication filtering — fetching exactly 8 and filtering to 3 is the classic RAG recall bug; trim to @TopK AFTER filtering, never before
Over-fetching is for audit logging; trim whenever convenient
TOP_N must always equal @TopK exactly
Over-fetching speeds up the DiskANN index; trim before filtering for latency
questions.explain: The procedure over-fetches 5x because permission/publication filters consume candidates, joins back for metadata, applies filters, and only then trims — ORDER BY s.distance ranks the filtered set so the final results reflect what the user may actually see.

questions.q: How does the chapter's hybrid retrieval fuse VECTOR_SEARCH and CONTAINSTABLE results?
options: A neural reranker applied to the union
It picks whichever list has more rows
Weighted average of cosine distances and BM25 scores
Reciprocal rank fusion: 1/(60+rank) per list, summed, with no score normalization — missing ranks get COALESCE(..., 1000)
questions.explain: The chapter uses reciprocal rank fusion — SUM(1.0/(60+rank)) across the vector and text lists — because RRF needs no score normalization between the two lists; the constant 60 dampens high ranks and COALESCE(...,1000) gives one-list-only chunks a small participation score.

questions.q: For RAG corpora under ~50K vectors, what does the chapter recommend instead of VECTOR_SEARCH?
options: Replace the VECTOR_SEARCH call with exact VECTOR_DISTANCE ranking — same procedure shape and filters, 100% recall, no index to maintain
Disable permission filtering
Shard the corpus across databases
Migrate to Pinecone immediately
questions.explain: Under ~50K vectors the chapter says to swap VECTOR_SEARCH for exact VECTOR_DISTANCE ranking: the procedure shape and filters stay the same, you get 100% recall, and there is no DiskANN index to maintain.

questions.q: What is the 'golden question set', and what does it catch?
options: A set of prompts for fine-tuning the LLM
Twenty to fifty representative questions with known-good answers, run through the full pipeline on a schedule — the end-to-end test of chunking, embeddings, index, retrieval, prompt, and model
The benchmark dataset from Chapter 20 used only for ANN recall
A list of security questions for access-control audits
questions.explain: The golden set (20–50 questions with known-good answers) runs the full pipeline on a schedule with quality scored by an LLM judge or human spot-check; when it degrades, per-stage metrics reveal which stage changed — it is the end-to-end test of the entire system.
